title: Implement multi-language / international support

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

body:
Requested by the maintainer (2026-11-11), filed by an agent. **Paused (`P?`)**: not open for work until the maintainer sets a priority.

**Goal:** CamCraft can be used in languages other than English, and behaves correctly for users in other locales.

**What it likely covers** (to be confirmed and broken down when the pause is lifted - nothing here is decided):
- **UI text:** every user-visible string (ribbon, tree, pages, dialogs, tooltips, status line, refusals and warnings from generators, verify and the post gate) comes from a translation catalogue instead of a literal in the code, with English as the source and fallback.
- **Language choice:** a setting to pick the language (and "follow the system"), stored with the user's preferences, applied without a restart if practical.
- **Fonts:** bundled fonts that cover the supported scripts (the current set under `assets/ui/fonts/`), under licences that need no attribution.
- **Numbers and units in the UI:** decimal separator and digit grouping per locale when *displaying and typing* values; mm/inch stays a document setting, not a language setting.
- **What must never be localised:** posted G-code, CL files, project files, machine (`.mch`) and post (`.cps`) files, MCP tool names and their JSON, log lines agents parse, and test goldens. A decimal comma must never reach a posted number.
- **Refusal and diagnostic text:** translated for the user, but each refusal keeps a stable name or code so tests, MCP clients and issue reports can match it in any language.
- **Tests:** structural/AccessKit tests should match by stable ids rather than English labels, so they hold in every language.
- **Contributing translations:** a file format and a workflow a contributor can use without building the app.

**Open questions for the maintainer:**
1. Which languages first?
2. Translation mechanism (e.g. Fluent, gettext-style catalogues, or a simple key/value file) - it adds a dependency, so it needs a decision.
3. Right-to-left scripts in scope or not?
4. Are the user guide and the documentation site (#688) part of this, or a separate issue?

Done means (once unpaused and broken down): the app runs fully in at least one language besides English, switching language changes every user-visible string, posted output is byte-identical in every language and locale, and a test pins each of those.

No effort label yet: this is an umbrella that will be split into sub-issues, each weighted then.
